findings.evidence: Trivial.lean:52-59 and FiniteTypeTrivial.lean:99-108 have identical MulEquiv bodies; PointsFunctor.lean:54 gives points = GrpCat.of (WithConv (H →ₐ[R] A)) and FiniteTypeTrivial.lean:41 gives trivial R = of R R with carrier R; FiniteTypeProduct.lean:74-77 shows the intended reuse pattern.
findings.fix: Define `noncomputable def trivialPointsMulEquiv := TrivialGroup.pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A)`, mirroring FiniteTypeProduct.pointsMulEquiv (FiniteTypeProduct.lean:77) which is defined as `AffineGroup.Product.pointsMulEquiv ...`. The derived _apply/_symm_apply/_mapValue/mapValue_..._symm_apply lemmas then follow from the corresponding TrivialGroup.pointsMulEquiv_* lemmas (Trivial.lean:62-128) rather than restating their proofs.
findings.issue: trivialPointsMulEquiv copies the entire MulEquiv (toFun/invFun/left_inv/right_inv/map_mul') verbatim from TrivialGroup.pointsMulEquiv (Trivial.lean:52). Since HopfAlgebra.points (H := trivial R) A is defeq to WithConv (R →ₐ[R] ↥A), the raw equivalence already covers this object.

summary: The new categorical unit/counit/initial-object API is genuinely new, but trivialPointsMulEquiv re-derives the existing TrivialGroup.pointsMulEquiv verbatim instead of reusing it, unlike the parallel FiniteTypeProduct wrapper which defers to the raw equivalence.
